name: Billing
description: Prepaid wallets and the ledger that IS their balance. The predecessor kept a mutable Wallet.balance column beside a Transaction table -- two truths that drift, and when they drift the customer is right and you cannot prove otherwise; here wallets.balance_minor is a ROLLUP over append-only wallet_entries, so the entries are the balance and nothing may write the number (docs/logic-decisions.md #3). Amounts are integer minor units (object_money.py), so a wallet holds dollars or satoshis or a gift-card unit without special cases. hook_wallet_entries gates debits by summing the ENTRIES rather than trusting the rollup -- a gate must be authoritative, and it documents the known check-then-append race honestly rather than pretending a reserve/capture system exists. system_wallet_replenish tops up from a saved card off-session, with the safeguard the predecessor also carried and most systems skip: a MONTHLY CAP, because autopay plus one runaway metering bug is a four-figure surprise, and a cap of zero (the default) means auto top-up is simply off. Declines -- especially the authentication-required kind an off-session charge cannot satisfy -- are reported for a human to act on, never retried in a loop that gets a processor account flagged. Plans, subscriptions and the period biller are the next slice; this one is the money container they will draw on. 0.2.0 adds the recurring half: billing_plans is a price book that VERSIONS FORWARD (an invoice must forever show the price it was billed under, so a change is a new row, never a rewrite of history customers already paid against), subscriptions carry billing_mode explicitly (wallet | subscription | hybrid -- guessing the mode from whether a plan has a base price breaks the moment someone sells a zero-base plan with a real contract), and system_billing_runner closes periods into invoices. Double-billing is the failure customers never forgive, so the runner is idempotent by provenance rather than by a dedup table: a marker on the invoice means a re-run after a crash raises nothing. The status ladder climbs BOTH ways -- paying restores service, because a ladder that only descends leaves a paying customer cut off -- and cancel-at-period-end runs service to the end of the paid period rather than billing someone for time they cannot use. 0.3.0 completes the metering half: usage_events (append, caller-supplied event_id deduped by hook -- retries are metering's number one corruption source and a timed-out client must not be billed twice), system_usage_rollup folding them into usage_summaries, and rating at period close via object_billing. Rating reads SUMMARIES, never raw events: allowances and tiers are properties of a period's total, so per-event rating charges the first calls at retail and never applies the included quantity -- and the bucket boundary means metering can start batching later without touching one line of pricing. Usage lines say what was used, what the plan included and what the overage cost, so a customer can CHECK a bill rather than only dispute it. A metric with usage but no price is charged nothing and REPORTED, because silently billing for something the plan never named is worse than the revenue, while silently dropping it hides a pricing gap. Events stamp our own cost, so margin per customer per metric is a fold rather than a spreadsheet.
